title: Boss: on call
summary: It is 3 a.m. and the dashboard is red. Build the tools that tell you what is wrong in seconds.

steps.title: The pager goes off
steps.body: Three tools for the on-call runbook: a health simulator that understands start periods, a triage report across all containers, and a memory pressure check from `docker stats`.

steps.title: Health with a start period
steps.prompt: Write `List<string> Health(List<bool> probes, int retries, int startProbes)`. Same rules as before (start `starting`; a pass → `healthy`, failures reset; `retries` consecutive failures → `unhealthy`), except that failures among the **first `startProbes` probes** do not count, **as long as no probe has passed yet** (once a probe passes, the start period is over).
starter: List<string> Health(List<bool> probes, int retries, int startProbes)
solution: List<string> Health(List<bool> probes, int retries, int startProbes)
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("slow start is forgiven", new List<string> { "starting", "starting", "starting", "healthy" }, Health(new List<bool> { false, false, false, true }, 2, 3));
Dojo.Eq("start period ends, then failures count", new List<string> { "starting", "starting", "starting", "unhealthy" }, Health(new List<bool> { false, false, false, false }, 2, 2));
Dojo.Eq("a pass ends the start period early", new List<string> { "healthy", "healthy", "unhealthy" }, Health(new List<bool> { true, false, false }, 2, 5));
Dojo.Eq("no start period", new List<string> { "starting", "unhealthy" }, Health(new List<bool> { false, false }, 2, 0));

steps.title: Triage every container
prompt: Write `List<string> Triage(List<string> rows)`. Each row is `NAME|RUNNING|EXITCODE|OOMKILLED|LASTLOG` (RUNNING and OOMKILLED are `true`/`false`; LASTLOG may contain anything except `|`).
- For each stopped one, add `NAME: ` + the diagnosis from the last lesson (OOM first, then `exec format error` in the log, then the exit-code table, else `app error (exit N): LASTLOG`).
- Sort the lines so the most urgent come first: OOM and architecture problems, then app errors and 125/126/127/139, then exit 0, 137 and 143. Within a group keep input order.
- If nothing is stopped, return `all running`.
solution: string Diagnose(int exitCode, bool oomKilled, string lastLog)
if (oomKilled) return "out of memory: raise --memory or reduce usage";
if (lastLog.Contains("exec format error")) return "wrong CPU architecture: rebuild for the host platform";
0 => "main process finished: keep the server in the foreground",
125 => "docker could not create the container: check the run flags",
127 => "command not found: check CMD/ENTRYPOINT and file name case",
137 => "killed by SIGKILL: docker kill or a stop timeout",
var items = new List<(int Group, string Line)>();
int group = oom || log.Contains("exec format error") ? 0 : code is 0 or 137 or 143 ? 2 : 1;
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoRows = new List<string> {
"web|true|0|false|",
"migrate|false|0|false|Applied 3 migrations",
"api|false|1|false|Unhandled exception. Npgsql.NpgsqlException: Failed to connect to db:5432",
"worker|false|137|true|",
"cron|false|143|false|",
"tool|false|127|false|exec ./run.sh: no such file or directory",
"arm|false|1|false|exec /app/server: exec format error" };
Dojo.Eq("mixed fleet", new List<string> {
"worker: out of memory: raise --memory or reduce usage",
"arm: wrong CPU architecture: rebuild for the host platform",
"api: app error (exit 1): Unhandled exception. Npgsql.NpgsqlException: Failed to connect to db:5432",
"tool: command not found: check CMD/ENTRYPOINT and file name case",
"migrate: main process finished: keep the server in the foreground",
"cron: stopped by SIGTERM" }, Triage(dojoRows));
Dojo.Eq("all running", new List<string> { "all running" }, Triage(new List<string> { "web|true|0|false|", "api|true|0|false|" }));
hints: Give every line a group number (0, 1, 2) and sort by it; LINQ's `OrderBy` is stable, so input order is kept within a group.

steps.title: Memory pressure from docker stats
steps.prompt: `docker stats --no-stream --format "{{.Name}}|{{.MemUsage}}"` prints lines like `api|481.5MiB / 512MiB`. Write `List<string> Pressure(List<string> lines, int percent)` that returns `NAME at P% of its memory limit` for each container whose usage is **at least** `percent`% of its limit, in input order (P is the whole-number percentage, rounded down). Units are `B`, `KiB`, `MiB`, `GiB` (powers of 1024); numbers may have decimals. Return `ok` alone if none qualify.
solution: if (p >= percent) result.Add($"{f[0]} at {p}% of its memory limit");
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoStats = new List<string> { "api|481.5MiB / 512MiB", "db|1.2GiB / 2GiB", "web|60MiB / 1GiB", "cache|1023.5MiB / 1GiB" };
Dojo.Eq("90% threshold", new List<string> { "api at 94% of its memory limit", "cache at 99% of its memory limit" }, Pressure(dojoStats, 90));
Dojo.Eq("50% threshold", new List<string> { "api at 94% of its memory limit", "db at 60% of its memory limit", "cache at 99% of its memory limit" }, Pressure(dojoStats, 50));
Dojo.Eq("mixed units", new List<string> { "tiny at 50% of its memory limit" }, Pressure(new List<string> { "tiny|512KiB / 1MiB" }, 50));
Dojo.Eq("nothing hot", new List<string> { "ok" }, Pressure(new List<string> { "web|60MiB / 1GiB" }, 80));
hints: Check longer unit names before `B`, because `MiB` also ends in `B`.
